contractEvidence.rule: Judge exact current repository hash from actual Store-card/detail pixels. reviews.name: Cloud Jacket
reviews.actualPixelFinding: This exact v5 hash is a real improvement over v4: the current pixels show a visible darker side plane, a shorter far sleeve, readable zipper/pocket hardware, rounded outer sleeves and a grounded shadow. Candy Core identity and card readability are clear. It still misses the premium Tier-4 bar when viewed beside accepted Tops 7-10 on the same contact sheet. The torso remains a stack of broad flat color bands, the supposed puffer cells do not visibly bulge or compress around the body, the hood reads as a large flat arch rather than a recessed padded opening, and rib-knit/fabric/metal differences are mostly graphic patterns and gradients rather than tactile material response. At card scale it still reads much closer to a polished vector icon than the coherent dimensional garment renders already accepted in this collection.
reviews.repairForProducer09: Keep the v5 asymmetry, Candy Core cloud/star identity, zipper/pockets and general silhouette, but change the rendering recipe rather than adding more SVG decoration. Make the torso and sleeves visibly padded in three dimensions: curved baffles wrapping around the body, seam compression, soft cloth thickness at edges, a recessed hood opening, attached sleeve volume and material-specific highlights/roughness. Match the same physical 3D cloth language already visible in accepted Tops 7-10 at Store-card scale; do not return a recolor or heavier-outline variant of this flat panel construction.

reviews.name: Star Coat
reviews.actualPixelFinding: This exact v5 hash also improves materially over v4: Adventure Club identity is immediate, the navy/burgundy/sand/gold hierarchy is coherent, the compass/star hardware is distinctive, the near/far sleeves differ, pockets and belt read clearly, and the lower panels now extend farther than the prior bomber-like silhouette. However the actual detail and card pixels still sit well below the accepted lower-tier Tops on physical rendering. The silhouette remains squat enough that the long-coat read is weak at card scale; front, side and tail panels are mostly hard-edged 2D shapes without convincing cloth thickness, drape, fold tension or layered overlap; the quilted insert looks like a printed pattern; and lighting is dominated by vector gradients/strokes rather than form-defining material response. Tier 5 must be the collection's strongest physical/material statement, not merely the most ornamented icon.
reviews.repairForProducer09: Preserve the v5 Adventure Club palette, compass/star identity, belt and pocket construction, but rebuild the final silhouette and rendering as a true long outerwear piece in the same dimensional language as accepted Tops 7-10: clearly longer hem/tails at card scale, unmistakable three-quarter torso depth, overlapping storm/yoke layers with thickness, actual quilted loft, woven fabric folds/tension and metal hardware catching distinct highlights. Use cast/contact shadow and form lighting to separate planes. Do not solve Tier 5 with extra badges, outlines or flat panel detail.
